:::{#thm-exponential-family-sufficient}
#### The sum of the statistic is sufficient in an exponential family

Let $\dsn{X} \siid \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam}$ be a
[sample](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample) of a
[discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv)
whose [distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-random-variable)
is in an [exponential family](#def-exponential-family)
with [natural parameter](#def-natural-parameter) $\natparam$
and [statistic](sufficiency.qmd#def-statistic) $\stat$.
Then the [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation)
$\sumin \statf{\Rvar_\iobs}$ is
[sufficient](sufficiency.qmd#def-sufficient) for $\natparam$.

:::

::: proof

The solution to @exr-sample-factorization,
worked in @sol-sample-factorization,
writes the joint [mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf)
as a function of $\natparam$ and the [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation),
times a function of the data alone.
That form is the one in the [factorization theorem](sufficiency.qmd#thm-factorization),
which proves the statement.

:::
